newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Santos strike set to continue after talks fail.
newsitem.headline: Santos strike set to continue after talks fail.

text.p: Administrative portworkers from the key Brazilian port of Santos failed to reach an agreement with the port authority CODESP to end a strike which is paralyzing the port, a labor tribunal official said.

"The position of the two sides is very antagonistic. At this point there is not the slightest possibility of reconciliation between the two sides," said the spokesman for the Sao Paulo Labor Tribunal.
The workers have been on strike since Tuesday in protest against CODESP's failure to consult unions about a switch to 24-hour operations at the port.
The main source of conflict was the length of the working day and the method of salary calculation, the official said.
"The judge exhorted the union to suspend the strike, even if only temporarily," he added. "They did not exclude the possibility."
The Santos Administrative Portworkers' Union was due to hold an assembly at 2000 local/2300 GMT at which they will decide whether to continue striking.
The labor tribunal has ordered both sides to present written proposals within 48 hours and a new audience was scheduled for July 10.

In a separate court, a judge ruled that those responsible for the strike will be fined 100,000 reais ($92,600) for every day during which they do not guarantee a minimum of 50 percent of operations, the official said.
